title: Reflection Symmetry of Gaussian (q-Binomial) Coefficients
description: The full reflection symmetry \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q for the Gaussian (q-binomial) coefficient over any CommSemiring, together with the dual q-Pascal recurrence it depends on. Resolves two of the three open-question items left by the parent entry (binomial-theorem-oq-02-oq-02-oq-01), which had proved only the k=1 special case. At q=1 the result recovers the classical Nat.choose_symm.

originalContributions: qBinomial_succ_succ_dual: the dual q-Pascal recurrence \binom{n+1}{k+1}_q = \binom{n}{k+1}_q + q^{n-k}\binom{n}{k}_q, valid for ALL n,k over an arbitrary CommSemiring. Over a CommSemiring this is NOT an algebraic rearrangement of the primal (defining) recurrence — with no subtraction available it must be proved by its own induction.

The dual recurrence is proved by induction on n: the generic interior step expands the left coefficient by the primal rule and rewrites the two resulting (n+1)-row coefficients by the inductive (dual) hypothesis, matching powers of q after destructuring n = j+1+m to clear the truncated natural subtraction in the exponent.

qBinomial_reflection: the full reflection symmetry \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q for k ≤ n. The interior step expands the left coefficient by the dual rule and the reflected coefficient by the primal rule; both produce the same power q^{n-j}, and the inductive hypothesis identifies the remaining two q-Pascal pieces.
qBinomial_reflection_add: the symmetric a+b form \binom{a+b}{a}_q = \binom{a+b}{b}_q, the q-analogue of Nat.choose_symm_diff.
qBinomial_reflection_at_one_eq_choose: at q=1 the q-reflection recovers the classical Nat.choose_symm, confirming the q-deformation is faithful.

Technique note: linear_combination is unavailable over a CommSemiring (it requires subtraction); the generic-step identity is instead discharged by targeted nth_rewrite of each q-Pascal row on only one side of the goal, followed by ring (which is valid over a CommSemiring).
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. All four theorems depend only on the standard foundational axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] (no sorryAx, no Lean.ofReduceBool). Builds on the parent's qBinomial API (imported from Proofs.BinomialTheoremOQ02OQ02OQ01).

overview.historicalContext: The Gaussian binomial coefficient \binom{n}{k}_q is a one-parameter deformation of the ordinary binomial coefficient, recovering Nat.choose at q=1. It satisfies two complementary q-Pascal recurrences (a 'primal' and a 'dual' form), and a reflection symmetry \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q — the q-analogue of the classical \binom{n}{k} = \binom{n}{n-k}. Combinatorially, \binom{n}{k}_q is the generating polynomial counting partitions fitting in a k×(n-k) box, and the reflection symmetry corresponds to transposing the box; geometrically it counts k-dimensional subspaces of 𝔽_q^n, dual to (n-k)-codimensional ones. Mathlib v4.26.0 has no Gaussian binomial API (only a TODO in Mathlib.RingTheory.Polynomial.Pochhammer), so the whole development is built from the recurrence in the parent entry.
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry binomial-theorem-oq-02-oq-02-oq-01 defines qBinomial over a CommSemiring via the primal q-Pascal recurrence and proves only the k=1 special case of reflection symmetry (qBinomial_reflection_at_one), explicitly listing the dual q-Pascal recurrence and the full reflection symmetry \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q as open future work. This entry proves both.
overview.proofStrategy: First establish the dual q-Pascal recurrence by induction on n (a genuinely separate induction, since over a CommSemiring it cannot be derived algebraically from the primal one). Then prove reflection symmetry by induction on n: in the interior column the left coefficient is expanded by the dual recurrence and the reflected coefficient by the primal recurrence, after which both reduce to the same power of q times the inductive hypothesis. The recurring obstacle — truncated natural subtraction in the q-exponents — is cleared by destructuring the strict inequality j < n as n = j+1+m, turning every exponent into a subtraction-free polynomial that ring can normalize.
keyInsights: Over a CommSemiring the dual q-Pascal recurrence is NOT a rearrangement of the primal one: the algebraic step (q^{k+1}-1)\binom{n}{k+1}_q = (q^{n-k}-1)\binom{n}{k}_q needs subtraction, which is unavailable, so the dual recurrence must be its own induction.

The reflection proof needs BOTH recurrences at once — dual on the left coefficient, primal on the reflected coefficient — so that the two surviving q-Pascal pieces become a matched pair the inductive hypothesis closes; using the same recurrence on both sides leaves an irreducible (q^a-1) obstruction.

Destructuring j < n as n = j+1+m is the key device for taming truncated ℕ-subtraction: it rewrites q^{n-j} as q^{m+1} and q^{n-(j+1)} as q^m, after which ring can combine powers (ring cannot reason about Nat.sub).

linear_combination requires a CommRing; to stay at CommSemiring generality the final algebraic identity is closed by nth_rewrite (applying each dual relation to a single side of the goal) followed by ring.

conclusion.summary: Proves the dual q-Pascal recurrence and the full reflection symmetry \binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n}{n-k}_q over an arbitrary CommSemiring, resolving two of the three open items flagged by the parent entry. 4 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: Reflection symmetry and the dual q-Pascal recurrence are core structural facts of the q-binomial calculus and prerequisites for the q-binomial theorem (Cauchy's identity) and finite-Grassmannian subspace counting — none of which are currently in Mathlib. Together with the parent's primal recurrence and q-Vandermonde base cases, this completes the elementary recurrence layer of a self-contained Gaussian-binomial API suitable for upstream contribution at Mathlib/Combinatorics/Enumerative/QBinomial.lean.
openQuestions: Full inductive q-Vandermonde identity \binom{m+n}{r}_q = ∑_{k} q^{(m-k)(r-k)} \binom{m}{k}_q \binom{n}{r-k}_q (the parent established only the m=0 and n=0 base cases).
q-binomial theorem (Cauchy): ∏_{i=0}^{n-1}(1 + q^i x) = ∑_{k=0}^{n} q^{k(k-1)/2} \binom{n}{k}_q x^k.
Combinatorial model: identify \binom{n}{k}_q with the generating polynomial of partitions inside a k×(n-k) box and read reflection symmetry off the box transpose.
